meta.notes: Most order-level reconciliation evidence comes from vendors selling reconciliation (Petpooja, UrbanPiper, Terra Insight, BillNote, restaurantdaily); news evidence (2025-2026) is mostly about unconsented ad/discount deductions rather than arithmetic settlement errors. Contradiction searches were run on platform transparency and error rarity; Swiggy's <1% claim, Petpooja's 'some find everything lines up' and the small-recovery estimate are included. No independent survey of time spent or error rates was found. Dispute windows conflict across sources (7-14 vs ~90 days). Cointab (cointab.in) failed TLS verification and a job posting on foundit.in returned 403; both were left out. Prospecting fell short: only 8 companies with fetchable own sites were found (target 20+); many small cloud kitchens have no site, JS-only sites or unresolvable domains. Contacts only for Kouzina (team page). Several prospects are larger than the 5-50 employee ICP band.

summary.statement: Without a POS that bundles reconciliation, restaurants download each aggregator's payout file and match it to POS sales by hand in spreadsheets, often through dedicated accounts staff.
Some restaurants catch errors only through periodic audits of their own accounts.
POS vendors (Petpooja, UrbanPiper, BillNote) and finance tools (Open Money) now automate order-level matching for their own users.
Unconsented ad, discount and fee deductions are widely and repeatedly reported in 2025-2026 by restaurants and associations in Bengaluru and Noida and on Reddit.
Order-level settlement errors (status mismatches, wrongly charged coupons) are described mainly by vendors selling reconciliation, with no measured error rate.
Counter-evidence: Swiggy says under 1% of partners are affected, Petpooja says some owners find payouts line up, and differences are small below 30-40 orders a day.
One estimate puts unrecovered discrepancies at ₹5,000-15,000 a year for ₹10 lakh/month of aggregator revenue, so per-outlet recoverable money may be small outside the large unconsented-charge cases.
Much of the reported loss is unconsented promotions and ad charges, not arithmetic errors, so an audit must check deductions against consent, not only orders against payouts.
Vendor estimates of manual reconciliation time range from 2-3 hours a week at 80+ daily orders to 3-5 hours, or half a day, a week for a multi-outlet chain.
The workload rises with outlets, platforms and brands per kitchen.
All time figures come from vendors; no independent survey of owners' time was found.
Disputes are raised as tickets in each platform's partner app, then escalated to account managers or partner WhatsApp groups.
Owners describe the process as slow and often abandoned: one chain took nearly two years to recover Rs 10 lakh, and one complaint was blocked by a dashboard error.
Dispute windows are reported inconsistently (7-14 days vs ~90 days), but vendors agree late queries risk being lost.
Alternatives are a contingency recovery service charging 10% of recoveries and collective association pressure, which won Swiggy refunds in Bengaluru.
In the one documented purchase, a restaurant co-founder drove the reconciliation tool choice after evaluating several vendors.
Mid-size operators have finance heads who may evaluate such tools.
Petpooja bundles order-level aggregator reconciliation into POSS at no extra cost; UrbanPiper and BillNote offer it inside their platforms.
Standalone options exist or are emerging: Open Money's agent, Terra Insight's TransactIG (roadmap), SideKyk (WhatsApp, waitlist), MYND's managed service and the GetMyRefund contingency service.

new_unknowns.question: What share of payout losses are order-level settlement errors versus unconsented ads, discounts and fees, and does the tool need consent records to catch the latter?
How much money per outlet per month is actually recoverable once structural deductions are excluded?
